description: People, places, legends, and supernatural laws associated with the Gambler's Folly.

entries.title: Veskan Faltreux
entries.summary: An audacious gambler and con artist whose final wager bound his essence to the Gambler's Folly.
body: Veskan was famous for impossible victories won through wit, deception, and luck. He believed the greatest games required risking everything, a creed that eventually led him to [[edge-of-fortune|the Edge of Fortune]].

There he accepted the [[keeper-of-chances|Keeper of Chances]] as an opponent in a game without cheating. Veskan lost his soul and became part of [[gamblers-folly|the Gambler's Folly]], where his laughter, groans, and mocking whispers are still heard when cards are drawn or the deck abandons a hesitant owner.

entries.title: The Keeper of Chances
entries.summary: An enigmatic being who wagers in pure luck and transformed Veskan Faltreux into a supernatural deck.
body: The Keeper appeared among the silent, star-eyed patrons of [[edge-of-fortune|the Edge of Fortune]]. It challenged [[veskan-faltreux|Veskan Faltreux]] to abandon tricks and stake his soul on chance alone.

Legends claim that anyone who draws every card of [[gamblers-folly|the Gambler's Folly]] and survives may earn an audience with the Keeper. Whether that meeting brings reward, punishment, or another wager remains unknown.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: The Gambler's Folly / Keeper of Chances

entries.title: The Edge of Fortune
entries.summary: A mysterious tavern of silent, star-eyed patrons where Veskan Faltreux wagered away his soul.
body: The Edge of Fortune is known only through the origin story of [[gamblers-folly|the Gambler's Folly]]. Its patrons concealed themselves in shadow and watched with eyes resembling stars.

Within the tavern, [[keeper-of-chances|the Keeper of Chances]] demanded a game governed by luck rather than deception. The establishment's location, permanence, and relationship to the Keeper are not recorded.

entries.title: Vanishing Laws of the Gambler's Folly
entries.summary: The deck demands regular use, warns its holder, and teleports away when left idle.
body: [[gamblers-folly|The Gambler's Folly]] refuses passive ownership. Its clock-faced case counts toward an uncertain deadline, while a growing glow warns that the deck expects another draw.

When neglected, the deck disappears despite containers or magical protection and seeks a new owner or discoverable hiding place. It favors gambling dens, taverns, ruins, treasure stores, and the belongings of travelers or merchants.
Suppression pauses its impatience only temporarily. Once free, the deck demands swift use, and traces of its departure can briefly lead pursuers toward its new location.

sections.heading: Legacy Timing and Retrieval
body: The source defines random day limits, a 24-hour post-suppression deadline, a seven-day tracking window, and an Arcana difficulty. These procedures require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Rules of the Gambler's Folly: The Vanishing Cards

entries.title: Reformation Law of the Gambler's Folly
entries.summary: Separated or destroyed pieces of the deck return intact to the last person who drew a card.
body: Cards removed from [[gamblers-folly|the Gambler's Folly]] lose their power until the deck is complete. The case and cards cannot be kept apart: distance, barriers, fire, loss into the Abyss, and deliberate scattering all fail to prevent reunion.

When multiple people hold different pieces, the complete deck reforms with the person who drew most recently. Witnesses may see a shimmer and hear [[veskan-faltreux|Veskan]] mock the attempt to defeat the deck's nature.

sections.heading: Legacy Reformation Procedure
body: The source assigns a 24-hour separation limit and an Arcana difficulty for recognizing the enchantment. These procedures require conversion.
